page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.14xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The system is built upon the x86_64 CPU architecture, providing 56 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 480.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile yields approximately 8.57 GB of RAM per vCPU, supporting expansive working datasets that demand high physical memory availability without CPU time-slicing contention.

Networking performance includes a baseline bandwidth allocation of 10 Gbps, maintaining consistent throughput for cluster operations. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external block storage for persistent filesystems and operating system volumes. Furthermore, the configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators, operating purely as a dense compute and memory execution target.

The dedicated processor allocation provides isolation against multi-tenant resource contention, stabilizing execution latency across long-running tasks. This resource balance provides high efficiency for workloads requiring large memory capacities relative to core count. Appropriate use cases include enterprise in-memory databases, massive distributed caching layers, analytical processing platforms, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.14xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by an x86_64 CPU architecture and executed via the KVM hypervisor. The server configuration provisions 56 dedicated vCPUs alongside 480.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 8.57 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, necessitating external block storage attachments for host operating system volumes and application data persistence. Network traffic is serviced with a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, ensuring predictable inter-node communication across cloud deployments. Due to its dedicated processor provisioning and high memory density, the instance delivers dependable execution without thread contention. These hardware characteristics make the server appropriate for running large in-memory caches, distributed processing engines, enterprise databases, and heavy real-time data transformation workloads.
